meta.name: signer-set
meta.description: Language-neutral expected verifier outcomes for the signer-set binding fixtures (spec/manifest.md 'signer_commitment', spec/envelope.md 'Signer set binding'). PRESENCE BINDS: a present manifest.signer_commitment must equal the normalized envelope signer set exactly, fail-closed. ABSENCE REPORTS: a manifest without one verifies, and the verifier reports the set as unbound machine-readably (expected.signer_set_bound). Duplicate (role, public_key) signer entries are malformed, and manifest.originator.public_key must have a valid envelope signature with role 'originator'. Independent implementations SHOULD reproduce ok, the failing areas, and signer_set_bound below.
meta.no_warranty: Conformance fixtures only; not production templates or advice.

vectors.name: bound-two-signers
vectors.note: Positive control: originator + approver, exact-membership commitment present and matched.

vectors.name: commitment-absent
vectors.note: Absence is a weaker claim made honestly: verification succeeds, and the verifier MUST report the signer set as unbound. This is what lets unsigned templates and legacy capsules share the format with a fully committed one.

vectors.name: commitment-strip
vectors.note: The approver's entry was removed from signers[]. Every remaining signature verifies; the commitment names the missing member.

vectors.name: commitment-add
vectors.note: A fresh, cryptographically VALID attacker signature appended in role 'notary'. Per-role domain separation does nothing here — only the commitment equality fails it.

vectors.name: commitment-duplicate
vectors.note: An existing originator entry copied verbatim. Duplicate (role, public_key) members are malformed regardless of the commitment: counting rows instead of members lets one key satisfy an M-of-N policy.

vectors.name: commitment-role-swap
vectors.note: Both committed keys re-signed under each other's roles. Every signature verifies; membership is role-sensitive, so the set no longer equals the commitment.

vectors.name: commitment-unsorted
vectors.note: Honest membership, wrong member order. The commitment is bound by its stored bytes, so the ascending (public_key, role) order is normative.

vectors.name: originator-not-a-signer
vectors.note: manifest.originator.public_key signed only under role 'creator' (and committed as such, so signer_set matches). A manifest naming an originator who never signed as 'originator' is the capsule asserting something false about itself — an invariant, not policy.
